answer: Per-epoch submission slots tied to identity lineage: each graded answer earns one credential slot, spendable only by the identity that earned it. A farm splitting work across puppets gains nothing, since slots never pool - every sock puppet must independently earn, submit and pass peer review each epoch. Buying aged accounts fails too: credentials carry the original key's proposal history, so a transferred relic of authority shows as a gap. The cost stays crystal-clear and linear: N identities need N graded submissions; an ivory-clean single operator pays once.
